page_notes: Page 136 of PIR (Volume I, 2nd edition) contains entries for Anteius and Antianus. The image shows two explicit legatus Augusti pro praetore attestations: one for P. Anteius Rufus (Dalmatia) and one for [.....]us Antianus (Pannonia inferior).

problems.issue: The exact_text 'Legatus Augusti pro praetore provinciae Dalmatiae a. 51' is slightly truncated. The full quote from the image is 'Legatus Augusti pro praetore provinciae Dalmatiae a. 51 t. 1—5'.
problems.suggested_fix: Update exact_text to 'Legatus Augusti pro praetore provinciae Dalmatiae a. 51 t. 1—5'.

problems.issue: The date_normalized_end is set to 51, but the text implies he held the post for multiple years (t. 1—5).
problems.suggested_fix: Set date_normalized_end to 55 or add a note clarifying the duration.

problems.issue: The office for the Syria appointment is marked as 'legatus Augusti pro praetore (designatus)', but the text states he was 'destinata' (designated) but never took office.
problems.suggested_fix: Clarify in notes that he was designated but did not assume the post.

problems.issue: The displayed_name '[.....]us Antianus' is correct, but the normalized_name 'Antianus' omits the partially lost nomen.
problems.suggested_fix: Update normalized_name to '[.....]us Antianus' or add a note about the partial name.

problems.issue: The date_text 'sub M. Aurelio' is inferred but not explicitly stated in the text. The image shows 'Imp. Caesaris M. Aureli!!!!!!', which suggests a dedication during Marcus Aurelius' reign but does not specify exact years.
problems.suggested_fix: Update date_text to 'sub Imp. Caesare M. Aurelio' and adjust date_normalized_start/end to reflect the broader range (161-180).

problems.issue: The exact_text 'legatus Aug. pr. pr. provinciae Pannoniae inferioris' is correct but omits the dedicatory context ('dedicavit pro salute, victoria et perpetuitate').
problems.suggested_fix: Update exact_text to include the full quote: 'legatus Aug. pr. pr. provinciae Pannoniae inferioris, dedicavit pro salute, victoria et perpetuitate Imp. Caesaris M. Aureli!!!!!!'.
